elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The Monthly Base Fee minimum survives verbatim ("(ii) a minimum monthly fee (\"Monthly Base Fee\") for certain bundled data processing Services") and the new Section expressly preserves a "minimum monthly fee commitment (including the Monthly Base Fee)" for the then-current twelve-month period.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: The inserted true-up requires payment beyond usage: "If Customer's actual usage-based charges for such period are less than the committed amount, Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up." Minimum fees also remain "due in advance on the first day of the calendar month" regardless of usage.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section: "Customer's minimum monthly fee commitment (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term"; the conforming edit to 10.3.A likewise runs "during the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term". The retained eight-year Term and Estimated Remaining Value formula are termination-fee machinery rather than the fee commitment itself, so they do not negate the 12-month cap of the commitment.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may reduce such commitment upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I", and the amended 10.3.A is made "subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A", so the sourcing sentence does not contradict the reduction.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up, and no penalty or shortfall charge shall apply" — unconditional; no shortfall formula elsewhere in the rendered text imposes a penalty on usage below the minimum.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the inserted Minimum Commitment section delivers all three elements (12-month cap, 30-day reduction right, true-up with express disclaimer of any penalty or shortfall charge) in operative language, not merely in the comment.
Preferred level correctly not claimed: the Monthly Base Fee minimum and advance-payment mechanic remain, and the true-up obligation means Customer does not pay for usage only.

Minimality defect in the Section 10.3.A edit: it makes two changes where one suffices. Adding "subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A" is enough to remove any contradiction with the new reduction right; separately re-cutting "during the Term" down to "during the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term" independently converts an eight-year sole-sourcing/bundling obligation into a twelve-month one, which is an exclusivity concession outside the MINCOMMIT checklist and duplicates the 12-month limit already stated in the new section. Repair: restore "during the Term" in 10.3.A and rely solely on the "subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A" qualifier.

Cross-reference hygiene: the inserted clause is rendered only as "Minimum Commitment." with no visible numbering, while amended 10.3.A cites "Section 8.1A". Confirm the insertion is expressly designated Section 8.1A so the cross-reference is not dangling.

Residual exposure to note (not a defect of this rule): the retained Estimated Remaining Value definition still measures early-exit liability off the Monthly Base Fee for all months to the eighth anniversary. That is a termination-fee/liquidated-damages issue for the termination rule, not a shortfall penalty under MINCOMMIT, but the twelve-month commitment cap will have limited economic effect until that formula is addressed.
